sources.citation: LinSuN. n.d. [2014]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Bhojpuri (Rautahat, Bara, Parsa, Chitwan, Nawalparasi, Rupandehi). Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 151 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; no mention of Musahar at all.

sources.citation: Sunuwar, Shushila (सुनुवार, शुशीला). 2014 [2070 BS]. सिरहा जिल्लाको लालपुर गा.वि.स.का मुसहर जातिका लोक गीतहरूको अध्ययन [A study of the folk songs of the Musahar caste of Lalpur VDC, Siraha district]. MA thesis, Central Department of Nepali, Tribhuvan University, Kirtipur. 56 pp. (in Nepali, Preeti font)
sources.note: No phonology content; folk-song texts in Devanagari with Nepali literary commentary on theme, rhythm and structure; nothing on word stress or tone.

sources.citation: Thakur, Indresh & Surya Prasad Yadav. 2014. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Maithili. Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 149 pp.
sources.note: No stress statement (sociolinguistic survey); identity evidence only: p. 3 'the Maithili language is spoken by Brahman (Tarai).. Dhanuk, Musahar/Sada, Dusadh/Pasawan.. castes as their mother tongue', and p. 104 lists 'Musar' among Maithili dialects ('Bajjika, Bantar, Barei, Barmeli, Dehati, Kawar, Kyabrat, Makrana, Musar, Tati, and Thenthi'). Bibliography cites Yadav 1986 'Acoustic correlates of word stress in Maithili'.

sources.citation: Subedi, Udhab Prasad. 2013. Verbal Morphology in English and Musahar. M.Ed. thesis, Department of English Education, Sukuna Multiple Campus, Indrapur, Morang (Tribhuvan University, Faculty of Education). xiii+44+6 pp.
sources.note: No phonology section. The only mention of stress is a scope exclusion, p.24 (sec. 2.5 Limitations, item iv): 'Phonological changes of stress, vowels or consonants of the addition of affixes were not analyzed.' Content is verbal affixation only (present -tai/-baichhiyai/-aichhiyai, past -lakai/-liyai, future -aiwala, progressive rahal, perfective -chhiya/-alchhiya, infinitive -aike khatir) with paradigms for ~40 verbs in practical romanization without stress or tone marks.

sources.citation: Luintel, Sharad Kumar (लुइँटेल, शरदकुमार). 2012 [2069 BS]. कक्षा ८ मा अध्ययनरत सरदारभाषी (बाँतर) विद्यार्थीहरूले स्तरीय नेपाली वाक्यगठनमा गर्ने त्रुटिहरूको अध्ययन [A study of the errors in standard Nepali sentence construction made by Sardar-speaking (Bantar) students of class 8]. M.Ed. thesis, Nepali Language Education, Faculty of Education, Tribhuvan University. 8+60 pp. (in Nepali, Preeti font)
sources.note: No phonology content. Chapter 3 is a contrastive sketch of Nepali vs Sardar (Bantar) sentence grammar: gender, number, person, tense and aspect marking with Bantar example sentences (verbs do not agree for gender/number; imperfective suffixes ऐ, एत, ऐत, इ, इत, वेत); ch.1 notes the language is confined to speech only and mixed. Nothing on sounds, stress (बलाघात) or tone.

sources.citation: Ethnologue: Languages of the World, entry 'Musasa' [smm] -- 14th ed. (Grimes 2001), 16th ed. (Lewis 2009), 17th ed. (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2013), 22nd ed. (Eberhard, Simons & Fennig 2019). Dallas: SIL International. Read via web.archive.org captures.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology or typology fields in any edition. 17th/22nd eds.: 'Dialects: Bantar. Similar to Kochila (Saptari) Tharu [thq]'; 'Writing: Unwritten'; 'It has been suggested but not documented that they may speak a sociolect of the larger language groups they live among: Maithili, Bhojpuri, Avadhi, and Kochila Tharu. Not listed in the 2001 Nepal census.' No source cited in any edition (2001-2025): no SIL survey underlies the entry.

sources.citation: Crooke, W. 1896. 'Musahar', in The Tribes and Castes of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh, vol. IV, pp. 12-38. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; ethnography of the UP/Bihar Musahars quoting Nesfield's ritual phrases 'in the Musahar language' (e.g. p. 24 'Bhagmagni maharin hito sohagin..', 'Autke' rice); no grammar, no phonology, no statement about which language they speak beyond calling the phrases 'Musahar language'.

sources.citation: Nesfield, John C. 1888. 'The Musheras of Central and Upper India'. Calcutta Review 86 (January 1888), pp. 1-53.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; says the isolated hill Musheras 'still speak a language of' their own ('his own Kolarian tongue, or in Hindi, if his own language has been forgotten') and quotes one prayer 'in the Mushera language'; no linguistic analysis.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for musa1263 'Musasa' (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Nothing; classification Bihari > Tharuic > Unclassified Tharu; only sources are Crooke 1896 (wordlist, 14 items), Meyer & Deuel 1999 and Guneratne 2002 ('comments on subclassification'); no grammar, phonology or sketch exists (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).
